description:
Re-scoped 2026-11-09 (user: "rewrite the page and ticket for tags"). Proposal page: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-gl6.4.html. Supersedes the static-area (BEAM region) design.

Today ptr_in_ranges (runtime/src/heap/ref_io.rs:68) tests each pointer against every from-space range, so a collection of a heap with N grafted gifts costs edges x N (release bench, N three-cell lists: 100 = 2.7x, 1000 = 14x, 10000 = 127x the one-block cost; bench in session scratchpad gl6/t4/bench). It exists only to recognise literals: static closures, halt continuations, static struct literals (.fz_static_struct_*, native_codegen/prim.rs, declared non-writable) and the nil slot (NIL_ATOM_REF_SLOT, ir_runtime.rs:60).

Requires fz-gl6.10 (the low nibble belongs only to the forwarding marker; kinds live only in high bits and side-band kind bytes) and a predecessor step, proposed on the page and filed on approval: static closures and halt continuations become program-wide read-only data objects (deleting the per-process tables, fz_get_static_closure, fz_get_halt_cont and its lazy fallback, AOT child aliasing, CompiledModuleConsts static fields).

This ticket: a literal bit travels with the kind. Spare bits: ref word bits 60-63 (arm64, kind at 56) / 61-63 (x86-64, kind at 57); kind bytes in struct fields, closure captures and map entries use 4 of 8 bits; ListLink has 2-3 spare above the alias bit. The bit is part of the kind type, so decoding and re-encoding a kind keeps it by construction. It is set only at literal-making sites: codegen materialising a static struct / static closure / halt continuation ref and writing child-literal kind bytes; the runtime's nil slot ref; and a field read from a literal parent (a scalar ref into a literal is a literal). Fresh heap allocations never set it.

Users of the bit: forward.rs cheney_forward_strict_bits (:31) / forward_heap_value (:231) / forward_any_value_ref_root scalar (:58) copy unless tagged; deep_copy.rs HeapView::contains (:40) becomes "share if tagged, copy otherwise"; any_value.rs is_proc_heap_list/map (:1299, :1309) test the bit.

Done when:
- No release-build path walks from_ranges per pointer. ptr_in_ranges / is_active_from_space_object survive only as a debug-build cross-check asserting: an untagged heap pointer lies in from-space, a tagged one does not, and none lies in to-space.
- Deleted: GcStats.from_ranges_walked and its telemetry field (always equal to blocks_released); Heap::current_heap_tagged_addr and current_heap_addr_for_kind (no callers); deep_copy_test's other-heap list case (no production path creates one); heap_test's Rust-static scalar case becomes a tagged-literal case.
- Tests: a heap unit test grafts many small gifts and collects, asserting every survivor is forwarded and every tagged literal is left in place; a field read from a tagged literal returns a tagged ref; a literal that lost its tag faults (read-only), shown by a should_panic or documented probe.
- The bench shows the 10000-gift collection near the one-block cost; record before/after in the commit.
- No fixture pin changes.
- Documentation in the same commit: every .agent/docs page, guide (guides/*.html), README.md section and fixture README that describes a mechanism this ticket changes or removes is rewritten to the present fact in the same commit, and a grep for the old names and phrases over .agent, guides, README.md and fixtures returns nothing. Full gate green (--workspace --all-targets plus doc tests, fixture matrix with --test-threads=1). Commit in Why / What changed / Verification form. No co-author trailer, no attribution line.
title: Literals carry a tag: the collector, deep copy and the formatter test one bit, not the from-space chain
